snippet:
This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool designed to help users quickly connect to the Feishu/Lark platform and enable efficient collaboration between AI Agents and Feishu/Lark. The tool encapsulates Feishu/Lark Open Platform API interfaces as MCP tools, allowing AI assistants to directly call these interfaces and implement various automation scenarios such as document processing, conversation management, calendar scheduling, and more.
## Preparation
### Creating a Feishu/Lark Application
Before using the lark-mcp tool, you need to create a Feishu/Lark application:
1. Visit the [Feishu Open Platform](https://open.feishu.cn/) or [Lark Open Platform](https://open.larksuite.com/) and log in
2. Click "Console" and create a new application
3. Obtain the App ID and App Secret, which will be used for API authentication
4. Add the necessary permissions for your application based on your usage scenario
5. If you need to call APIs as a user, set the OAuth 2.0 redirect URL to http://localhost:3000/callback
For detailed application creation and configuration guidelines, please refer to the [Feishu Open Platform Documentation - Creating an Application](https://open.feishu.cn/document/home/introduction-to-custom-app-development/self-built-application-development-process#a0a7f6b0).
### Installing Node.js
Before using the lark-mcp tool, you need to install the Node.js environment.
**Using the Official Installer (Recommended)**:
1. Visit the [Node.js website](https://nodejs.org/)
2. Download and install the LTS version
3. After installation, verify in the terminal:
```bash
node -v
npm -v
```

### Domain Configuration
Based on your usage scenario, lark-mcp supports configuring different domain environments:
**Feishu (China Version)**:
- Default uses `https://open.feishu.cn` domain
- Suitable for users in China
**Lark (International Version)**:
- Uses `https://open.larksuite.com` domain
- Suitable for overseas users or international version of Lark
To switch to the international version of Lark, add the `--domain` parameter in your configuration:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"-y",
"@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",
"mcp",
"-a",
"<your_app_id>",
"-s",
"<your_app_secret>",
"--domain",
"https://open.larksuite.com"
]
}
}
}
```

The MCP tool supports a wide range of command parameters, allowing flexible configuration for suitable MCP startup commands. Detailed usage instructions for each parameter are provided below in **Parameter usage examples**.
## Prerequisites
The lark-mcp tool must be installed. Installation steps are as follows:
1. Run the following command in your local terminal to install lark-mcp.
```
npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g
```
**
If the terminal returns the message `It is likely you do not have the permissions to access this file as the current user`, you need to run the command as an administrator:`sudo npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp@beta -g`.
2. Run `lark-mcp -V` to check the MCP version.
If the version is lower than 0.4.0, it is recommended to uninstall and reinstall lark-mcp:
1. Uninstall lark-mcp: `npm uninstall @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g`
2. Reinstall lark-mcp: `npm install @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp -g`
3. Run `lark-mcp -V` again to verify the version information.
3. (Optional) Globally install OpenAPI MCP.
There are two installation methods for the MCP tool: global installation and NPX installation. You can use either method to use the tool. Choose the installation method that suits your actual needs.
After installing lark-mcp locally, you can use the MCP tool persistently (supported command parameters are referred to in the **Command Parameters** section below). Taking [Trae](https://www.trae.com.cn/) as an example, the global installation steps are explained as follows:
- Global installation: installs to a global path (/usr/local/lib), commands are persistent, and system-level commands are available. Suitable for scenarios where command line tools are used frequently.
- NPX installation: described in the [Install and use OpenAPI MCP](/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/mcp_integration/mcp_installation) document. This method allows quick installation and use, but the command is not persistent as it is installed in the system's temporary cache, deleted after execution. Suitable for quick trials or one-time usage.
1. Complete the preparatory work.
For details, see [Install and use OpenAPI MCP](/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/mcp_integration/mcp_installation#1cd67c23).

3. Open the terminal within the tool.

```

```

title: Install and use document search MCP - Lark CLI - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
### Install lark-mcp tool
lark-mcp is an MCP toolkit provided by the Lark Open Platform. You need to install lark-mcp (version 0.3.0 or higher) before using the document search MCP tool.
1. Open the command line in the Trae environment and execute the following command to globally install the lark-mcp tool.
- You can open the Terminal in Trae to execute the command, or you can open the command line of the operating system where Trae is located to execute the command. There is no difference between the two.
- The following command installs the latest version of lark-mcp by default. If your previously installed lark-mcp version is lower than 0.3.0, you need to re-execute the command to install the latest version of lark-mcp.
```
npm install -g @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp
```
2. After installation, execute the following command to check the installation status.
```
lark-mcp -V
```
If successful, the version number of the tool will be returned.
## Install document search MCP
Add MCP Server and install document search MCP tool in the AI tool (use [Trae](https://www.trae.ai/) as an example).
Some AI tools support one-click installation via URL, for example: [![Install MCP Server](https://cursor.com/deeplink/mcp-install-dark.svg?height=28&lazyload=true&width=126)](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=lark_open_doc_search&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyIteSIsIkBsYXJrc3VpdGVvYXBpL2xhcmstbWNwIiwicmVjYWxsLWRldmVsb3Blci1kb2N1bWVudHMiXX0=)
1. Open the Trae tool.
2. Click the **Toggle AI Side Bar** icon in the upper right corner of the interface.
3. In the AI Sidebar's **AI management**, click **MCP**.
4. In the **MCP** interface, click **Add MCP Server**.
5. Click **Configure Manually**.
6. In the **Configure Manually** input box, replace the default content with the following content, and click **Confirm**.
```
{  "mcpServers": {    "lark_open_doc_search": {      "command": "npx",      "args": [        "-y",        "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",        "recall-developer-documents"      ]    }  }}
```
7. The system will prompt that the MCP tool has been automatically added to **@Builder with MCP**. Click **Got it**.
After configuration is complete, you can view the MCP tool (named lark_open_doc_search) on the **MCP Servers** page.

# Use lark-mcp in Docker (Alpha)
This document describes how to build and run the official lark-mcp Docker image with built-in keytar secure storage, ready to use out of the box.
## Prerequisites
- Docker Desktop installed (or any Docker runtime)
- Your Feishu/Lark application App ID and App Secret
## 1) Build the image
```
# Execute from project root directory
docker build -t lark-mcp:latest .
```

### stdio Mode Configuration
If using the default stdio mode, add the following to your MCP client (e.g., Cursor) configuration file:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "docker",
"args": [
"run", "--rm", "-i",
"-v", "lark_mcp_data:/home/node/.local/share",
"lark-mcp:latest", "mcp",
"-a", "your_app_id",
"-s", "your_app_secret"
]
}
}
}
```
### streamable Mode Configuration
If using streamable (HTTP) mode, first start the container:
```
docker run --rm -it \
-p 3000:3000 \
-v lark_mcp_data:/home/node/.local/share \
lark-mcp:latest mcp -a <your_app_id> -s <your_app_secret> -m streamable --host 0.0.0.0 -p 3000
```
Then add the following to your MCP client configuration file:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp"
}
}
}
```
### User Identity Configuration (user_access_token)
> ⚠️ **Important Note**: In Docker environment, OAuth mode does not support yet. Please use -u for user authentication.
1. **MCP client configuration**:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"lark-mcp": {
"command": "docker",
"args": [
"run", "--rm", "-i",
"-v", "lark_mcp_data:/home/node/.local/share",
"lark-mcp:latest", "mcp",
"-a", "your_app_id",
"-s", "your_app_secret",
"-u", "your_user_access_token",
"--token-mode", "user_access_token"
]
}
}
}
```

# Call Lark MCP server in remote mode (Deprecated)
Last updated on 2026-04-23
Lark Open Platform provides a remote MCP Server configuration feature that supports the Streamable HTTP transmission protocol, allowing users to securely and efficiently integrate and use rich Lark open capabilities in cloud scenarios with AI agents such as Cursor, Trae, Claude, and n8n via one-click integration.
## Configuring the MCP Server
Create a remote MCP service on the Lark MCP Configuration Platform and customize tools (i.e., Lark Open Platform server-side APIs) to flexibly build the MCP tools your business needs.
**
All tools are called via API under the identity of the currently logged-in user (user_access_token). Details:
- During the configuration process, the system guides you to complete the authorization operation for the logged-in user with one click. The MCP Server can only call tools on behalf of the user after authorization.
- The user_access_token itself has an expiry time. The remote MCP Server configuration feature supports automatic refreshing of the token before expiration.
- For more on user_access_token, see [Obtaining user_access_token](/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/get-user-access-token) and [Refreshing user_access_token](/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/refresh-user-access-token).
1. Log in to the [Lark MCP Configuration Platform](https://open.larksuite.com/page/mcp).
**
The remote MCP Server configuration function is in internal testing. If you cannot access the configuration platform, you can contact the customer success manager to activate the internal testing.
2. On the left side of the page, click **New MCP Service**.
3. On the service creation page, complete the following configurations.
1. In the **MCP tool settings** area, confirm the current user identity.
When using MCP to manage Lark business resources, the current displayed user will be used. Therefore, confirm the current user identity is correct; if not, log out and log back in with the correct user.
2. In the **Add Tools** card, click **Add**.
3. In the **Add tools** dialog, choose the needed tools.
The platform provides **Ready-Made Toolkits** for selection. If none meet your needs, you can flexibly select various tools from the **Tailored Tools** list. For example, if your business needs MCP to manage Lark Multidimensional Tables, select Multidimensional Tables.
